entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Su Hui (蘇蕙, courtesy name Ruolan 若蘭), a prominent female poet of the Former Qin dynasty (351–394 CE) during China's turbulent Sixteen Kingdoms period, stands as a singular figure in classical Chinese literature, renowned for pioneering the complex genre of the palindrome poem. Flourishing in an era marked by political fragmentation and cultural synthesis following the collapse of the Western Jin, Su Hui transcended the limitations often imposed on women in her society, creating a work of unparalleled structural ingenuity. Her most celebrated creation, the "Xuanji Tu" (織錦回文, "Picture of the Weaving Loom" or "Brocade of Interlocked Rings"), represents not merely a poetic achievement but a mathematical and linguistic marvel, cementing her legacy as an innovator whose work continues to challenge and fascinate scholars and readers across millennia.

The "Xuanji Tu" is a unique 29 x 29 character grid, comprising 841 characters (not 7,848 as sometimes misstated in legend) woven into a brocade, which, according to tradition, Su Hui created for her husband, Dou Tao, a prefect of Qinzhou, after he was exiled to the desert or took a concubine. The poem is a tour de force of literary craftsmanship, designed to be read in multiple directions – forward, backward, horizontally, vertically, and diagonally – yielding hundreds, possibly thousands, of distinct poems expressing longing, sorrow, and fidelity. This intricate structure required an extraordinary command of language and an innovative approach to poetic form, pushing the boundaries of what was considered possible in classical Chinese verse. Its creation in a period of significant intellectual and artistic ferment highlights the resilience of cultural production amidst political upheaval.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Su Hui's creation of the "Xuanji Tu" was a singular achievement in classical Chinese poetry, establishing the complex palindrome poem genre and influencing literary craftsmanship for centuries. Her work became a subject of intense scholarly interest and cemented her legacy as an intellectual innovator.
